people.name: Omarion
people.description: Omarion, US R&B singer, (Omari Ishmael Grandberry), former B2K singer, 2005 US No.1 album 'O' and 2006 US No.1 album ‘21.’

people.name: Nick D'Virgilio
people.description: American musician and singer Nick D'Virgilio, best known as a member of the progressive rock band Spock's Beard. He was also one of two drummers chosen to replace Phil Collins in Genesis on the Calling All Stations album. He has performed session work with many artists, including Tears for Fears.

people.name: Jo Dunne
people.description: Jo Dunne, bassist from English alternative rock group We've Got A Fuzzbox And We're Gonna Use It who had the 1989 UK No.11 single 'International Rescue'.

people.name: Vic Chesnutt
people.description: Vic Chesnutt, American singer-songwriter. Chesnutt who died on Dec 25th 2009 released 17 albums during his career, including two produced by Michael Stipe.

people.name: David Ellefson
people.description: American musician David Ellefson, bassist with Megadeth, from 1983–2002 and 2010–2021. They had the 1990 UK No.13 hit single with a cover of the Alice Cooper song 'No More Mr Nice Guy'. Megadeth are known for their technically complex guitar work and musicianship and is one of the "big four" of American thrash metal bands along with Slayer, Anthrax, and Metallica and is credited with helping to develop and popularise the genre. Ellefson co-founded the hard rock band Lucid in 2021.

people.name: Les McKeown
people.description: Les McKeown, Scottish singer of the 1970s pop group, Bay City Rollers who had the 1975 UK No.1 single 'Bye Bye Baby' plus 11 other UK Top 20 singles and the 1976 US No.1 single 'Saturday Night'. The Rollers were also the subject of a 20-week UK television series, Shang-a-Lang. McKeown died on 20 April 2021 age 65.

people.name: Calum Macdonald
people.description: Calum Macdonald, Runrig, (1995 UK No.18 single 'An Ubhal As Airde, The Highest Apple').

people.name: Laurence Juber
people.description: Laurence Juber, British guitarist, most famous for playing lead guitar with Paul McCartney in Wings.

people.name: Arthur Tavares
people.description: Arthur Tavares, from American R&B, funk, and soul group Tavares, who had the 1976 UK No.4 and US No.15 single 'Heaven Must Be Missing An Angel'. He died on 15 April 2024.

people.name: Errol Brown
people.description: Errol Brown, singer, Hot Chocolate, who had the 1975 US No.3 single 'You Sexy Thing' the 1977 UK No.1 single 'So You Win Again' and over 25 other Top 40 hits. Hot Chocolate started their recording career making a reggae version of John Lennon's 'Give Peace a Chance', and was contacted by Apple Records, saying that Lennon liked this version, and the group was subsequently signed to Apple Records. Brown died of liver cancer at his home in the Bahamas on 6 May 2015.

people.name: Donald Roeser
people.description: Donald Roeser, from American hard rock band Blue Oyster Cult who scored the 1976 US No.12 & 1978 UK No.16 single '(Don't Fear) The Reaper'. Blue Oyster Cult have sold over 24 million records worldwide.

people.name: Neil Young
people.description: Neil Young, Canadian singer, songwriter and guitarist who as a member of Buffalo Springfield had the 1967 US No.17 single 'For What It's Worth'. Joined Crosby, Stills Nash & Young who had the 1970 US No.1 and UK No.5 album DejVu. As a solo artist Young scored the 1972 US No.1 and UK No.10 single Heart Of Gold, and his 1972 UK No.7 album Harvest spent 66 weeks on the UK chart. In 2008 a newly discovered trapdoor spider Myrmekiaphila neilyoungi was named after the singer.

people.name: Booker T Jones
people.description: Booker T. Jones. Booker T and the MG's, who had the 1962 US No. 3 single 'Green Onions', and the 1969 UK No.4 single 'Time Is Tight'. Booker T. played keyboards on the Otis Redding hit '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay'.

people.name: John Maus
people.description: John Walker, (John Joseph Maus), vocals, best known as the founder of The Walker Brothers, (1966 UK No.1 & US No. 13 single 'The Sun Ain't Gonna Shine Anymore'). Walker died of liver cancer at his Los Angeles home, on 7 May 2011.

people.name: Brian Hyland
people.description: Brian Hyland, US singer, (1960 US No.1 & UK No.8 single 'Itsy Bitsy Weenie Yellow Polka Dot Bikini').

people.name: Screaming Lord Sutch
people.description: Screaming Lord Sutch, singer, politician and leader of The Official Monster Raving Loony Party. He was the first long-haired pop star - boasting hair over 18 inches long. His early records included Jack The Ripper and I'm A Hog For You Baby, he died on June 16th 1999. The self-styled lord - real name David Sutch - was Britain's longest-serving political leader, standing in nearly 40 elections.

people.name: Terry "Buzzy" Johnson
people.description: Terry "Buzzy" Johnson, American singer, songwriter and music producer who was a member of The Flamingos and a staff member of Motown Records where he and Smokey Robinson were regular collaborators. Johnson died in Las Vegas on October 8, 2025, at the age of 86.

people.name: Mort Shuman
people.description: American singer, pianist and songwriter, Mort Shuman. He wrote many early 60s hits with Doc Pomus including 'Viva Las Vegas', 'Sweets For My Sweet', 'Teenager In Love', and 'Save The Last Dance For Me.' Shuman died of cancer on November 2, 1991.

people.name: Jo Stafford
people.description: American pop singer Jo Stafford. Her biggest hit the 1952 'You Belong To Me', topped the charts in both the US and the UK and the song became the first by a female singer to top the UK Singles Chart. She appeared in television specials including two series called The Jo Stafford Show, in 1954 in the US and in 1961 in the U.K. She died aged 90 on 16 July 2008.

works.title: Happy Together
works.eventDescription: Jim Tucker the original rhythm guitarist with American rock band The Turtles died age 74. He played with The Turtles from 1965 to 1968 and was featured on many of the band’s biggest hits, including the chart-topping 1967 classic 'Happy Together,' plus 'She’d Rather Be with Me' and the group’s 1965 cover of Bob Dylan's 'It Ain’t Me Babe.'

works.title: The Heavy Entertainment Show
works.eventDescription: Robbie Williams broke the record for the most No.1 albums by a British solo artist. The singer's latest album, The Heavy Entertainment Show, debuted at No.1 on this week's chart. It is his 12th album to reach the summit and pushed him ahead of David Bowie who has 11 No.1 albums to his name.

works.title: If I Were a Boy
works.eventDescription: American singer Beyoncé released her third studio album I Am... Sasha Fierce debuting at No.1 on the US Billboard chart. Her third consecutive US No.1 solo album was marketed with the release of several singles, including 'If I Were a Boy' and 'Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)', both of which charted highly internationally. The former topped the charts in over ten countries. The album was titled I Am... Sasha Fierce to showcase the difference between Beyoncé and her alter ego Sasha Fierce; the first disc is titled I Am... while the second is titled Sasha Fierce.

works.title: Le Freak
works.eventDescription: American session drummer Tony Thompson died of cancer aged 48. He was most famous as the drummer with The Power Station along with Robert Palmer, and John Taylor and Andy Taylor of Duran Duran and Chic, whose single 'Le Freak' hit No.1 in the US, and No.7 in the UK. He also played on David Bowie's hit single 'Let's Dance'. Thompson also played drums with Led Zeppelin (along with Phil Collins) at Live Aid in 1985.

works.eventDescription: Die-hard Beatles fans were enraged after Paul McCartney altered the song writing credits on his 'Back In The US 2002' album, changing them to McCartney and Lennon from Lennon and McCartney.

works.title: Torn
works.eventDescription: Winners at the MTV Europe Awards included Madonna Best Female Artist and album for Ray Of Light, The Spice Girls won Best Group, All Saints won Breakthrough Artist, Robbie Williams, Best Male Artist and Natalie Imbruglia won Best Song with 'Torn.'

works.title: Ray of Light

works.title: Spiceworld
works.eventDescription: The Spice Girls were at No.1 on the UK album chart with their second album 'Spiceworld', it was also the name of their tie-in film. The album became a huge hit worldwide, lengthening the so-called "Spicemania" fever at that time. It produced 4 singles all of which saw commercial success and has now sold over 20 million worldwide.

works.title: Rattle and Hum
works.eventDescription: U2 started a six-week run at No.1 on the US album chart with their sixth studio album 'Rattle And Hum' which went on to sell over 14 million copies.

works.title: Infidels
works.eventDescription: Bob Dylan's Infidels album reached its highest position when it peaked at No.9 in the UK chart. Dylan's 22nd studio album was co-produced with Dire Straits guitarist Mark Knopfler. Dylan had also approached Elvis Costello, David Bowie and Frank Zappa as possible producers.

works.title: God Save the Queen
works.eventDescription: The Sex Pistols went to No.1 on the UK album chart with their debut LP Never Mind The Bollocks, Here's The Sex Pistols. the punk group's only No.1 album. The album was met by a hail of controversy upon its release. The first problems involved the allegedly 'obscene' name of the album, resulting in the prosecution of the manager of the Nottingham Virgin record shop for having displayed it in a window. More outrage was sparked by the lyrics of the songs 'God Save the Queen' and 'Anarchy in the UK.'

works.title: Let's Roll Another One

The set list for these early Floyd shows included: 'Let's Roll Another One', 'Gimme A Break', 'Interstellar Overdrive', 'Astronomy Domine' and 'Stoned Alone'. 'Stoned Alone' was also known as 'I Get Stoned', and was possibly the first song Syd Barrett wrote for Pink Floyd.

As a solo artist Young scored the 1972 US No.1 and UK No.10 single Heart Of Gold, and his 1972 UK No.7 album Harvest spent 66 weeks on the UK chart. In 2008 a newly discovered trapdoor spider Myrmekiaphila neilyoungi was named after the singer.

works.title: The Sun Ain’t Gonna Shine Anymore
works.eventDescription: John Walker, (John Joseph Maus), vocals, best known as the founder of The Walker Brothers, (1966 UK No.1 & US No. 13 single 'The Sun Ain't Gonna Shine Anymore'). Walker died of liver cancer at his Los Angeles home, on 7 May 2011.

works.title: Jack the Ripper
works.eventDescription: Screaming Lord Sutch, singer, politician and leader of The Official Monster Raving Loony Party. He was the first long-haired pop star - boasting hair over 18 inches long. His early records included Jack The Ripper and I'm A Hog For You Baby, he died on June 16th 1999. The self-styled lord - real name David Sutch - was Britain's longest-serving political leader, standing in nearly 40 elections.

works.title: You Belong to Me
works.eventDescription: American pop singer Jo Stafford. Her biggest hit the 1952 'You Belong To Me', topped the charts in both the US and the UK and the song became the first by a female singer to top the UK Singles Chart. She appeared in television specials including two series called The Jo Stafford Show, in 1954 in the US and in 1961 in the U.K. She died aged 90 on 16 July 2008.
